# Govern tool access

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) Sidecar governs which tools an AI agent can discover and call in Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric. It applies per-tool policy and holds protected calls for human approval before Envoy routes them to an MCP server. Tool servers keep responsibility for what each tool does.

@include '../../../global/partials/alerts/beta.mdx'

To set up the MCP Sidecar, refer to [Configure the MCP Sidecar](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access/configure).

@include 'alerts/enterprise-alert.mdx'

## Introduction

An agent can see a tool without having permission to run every operation it exposes. Consul Agentic Runtime Fabric checks each layer separately: catalog visibility, network connectivity, delegated user authority, tool policy, and human approval. Passing one check does not skip the others.

When you annotate an agent pod with the `ai-agent` role, Consul injects the MCP Sidecar. The agent pod then contains the following parts:

| Part | Role | Default port |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Envoy sidecar proxy | Carries mesh traffic and routes approved tool calls | `20000` |
| MCP listener | Receives the agent's tool calls on loopback at `/mcp` | `15101` |
| MCP Sidecar governance interceptor | The first filter on the MCP listener. Consul rejects every tool call when nothing listens on its port. | `21101`, loopback |
| On-behalf-of identity processor | Exchanges the user's token for a token scoped to the MCP server. Runs in the MCP Sidecar. | — |
| Approval server | Receives approval requests and returns a verdict, over plain HTTP on loopback | `16101` |

## How it works

1. The agent sends an MCP request, such as a tool discovery request or a tool call, to the MCP listener at `localhost:15101/mcp`.
1. The governance interceptor, the first filter on the listener, processes the request.
1. If the request includes the `x-mcp-hitl` header, Consul sends an approval request to the approval server and holds the call until it receives a verdict.
1. Consul allows the call only if a service intention allows this agent to call this tool on the MCP server.
1. When the call carries user context, the on-behalf-of identity processor exchanges the user's token for a token scoped to the MCP server. Refer to [On-behalf-of delegation](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/identity).
1. Envoy routes the approved call to the MCP server. An in-mesh server receives it over the service mesh. An external server receives it through a terminating gateway.
1. The MCP server applies its own identity and tool policy, then runs the tool.

The [Govern tool access](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/architecture#govern-tool-access) diagram on the architecture page shows this flow.

## Discovery and invocation

The sidecar returns a catalog of the tools the agent is allowed to see. A discovery response is not a credential or a lasting authorization. Policy can change between discovery and a call, so the sidecar evaluates every call when it happens.

The sidecar bases its decisions on validated request content and trusted configuration only. It does not accept caller-supplied headers as proof of authorization or human approval.

You define tool policy with service intentions. Each allow permission names the MCP server as the destination, the agent as the source, the HTTP path `/mcp`, and the tool name in the `x-mcp-tool` header. A call that no intention allows is rejected. Refer to [Define tool policy](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/tool-access/configure#define-tool-policy).

## Human approval

Human approval runs for tool requests that include the `x-mcp-hitl` header. Requests without the header skip approval. For a request that needs approval, Consul sends an approval request to the approval server in the agent pod and blocks the call until it receives a verdict. Your application owns the human interaction, such as showing the request to a person and collecting a decision.

The approval is bound to the exact action: the operation, destination, arguments, and request challenge. The sidecar rejects the call in the following cases:

- No verdict arrives before the approval timeout, which defaults to `60s`.
- The approval server is missing or unreachable.
- The verdict is a rejection.
- The approval is for a different tool, different arguments, or a different destination.

Destination policy still applies after approval. The sidecar enforces the decision but does not judge whether the person's decision is correct.

## Backend connectivity

| Backend | Path | What else applies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| In-mesh MCP server | Mesh route to the server. Consul adds an MCP router filter to the server pod's inbound Envoy listener. | The server applies its own identity and tool policy. |
| External HTTP MCP server | Route through a terminating gateway | The gateway adds a trusted credential and verifies external TLS. Refer to [External credential injection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/credential-injection). |

A provider credential authenticates the terminating gateway to the external server. It does not replace the caller's permission to call the tool.

## Observability

MCP Sidecars [automatically instrument supported tool exchanges](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation), so agents and tool servers do not need tracing SDKs. Decision logs record bounded metadata, never tool arguments, tool results, credentials, or approval tokens. Payload traces that capture arguments or results need the [payload-trace privacy controls](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/observability/auto-instrumentation#payload-span-sensitive-data-security).

Sidecar traces also feed [cycle detection](/consul/docs/agentic-mesh/cycle-detection), which finds agents that repeat the same tool call with the same arguments and unchanged results.

## Limitations

- A successful HTTP or MCP response means the protocol exchange succeeded, not that the user's task is complete.
- If the agent disconnects, an action that a backend already ran is not cancelled.
- Cycle detection runs asynchronously. It does not replace tool policy or human approval.
- Session handling and catalog aggregation can differ between topologies.
- Consul stores per-agent tool-call rate limits that you set on the service definition, but the sidecar proxy does not enforce them.
